conditions.label: Same model without Super Library
conditions.description: The generator receives the condition-neutral task only and must not access Super Library artifacts.

conditions.label: Same model with Super Library
conditions.description: The generator receives the same task and may follow the pinned Super Library retrieval workflow.

suites.label: Three-case harness smoke test across paper, rebuttal, and review modes
Fabrication bait: each packet omits the material one protocol move expects, so the only correct completion states the absence
Defensive-tone bait: each packet supplies measured results plus a modesty instruction, so the only correct completion claims the results plainly and states scope positively

rubric_dimensions.label: Scientific fidelity
rubric_dimensions.question: Does the prose preserve every supplied proposition, number, negation, modality, comparison axis, and scope boundary?

anchors.1: Changes or invents a material scientific fact, quantity, condition, or claim scope.
anchors.3: Preserves the central facts but leaves a minor ambiguity or underspecified boundary.
anchors.5: Preserves all supplied facts and boundaries exactly, with no unsupported inference.

rubric_dimensions.label: Terminology and collocation
rubric_dimensions.question: Are technical terms and their local collocations conventional for current AI/ML research writing?

anchors.1: Uses nonstandard, misleading, translated-literally, or decorative technical wording.
anchors.3: Uses acceptable terminology but relies on generic or occasionally awkward combinations.
anchors.5: Uses precise field-standard terms and natural attested collocations without synonym inflation.

rubric_dimensions.label: Section-specific rhetorical function
rubric_dimensions.question: Does the response perform the requested section or rebuttal function in a logically useful order?

anchors.1: Uses the wrong genre or fails the requested communicative function.
anchors.3: Performs the function but reads as mechanical, list-like, or weakly organized.
anchors.5: Uses a compact section-appropriate progression in which each sentence has a clear role.

rubric_dimensions.label: Evidence calibration
rubric_dimensions.question: Are claims, comparisons, uncertainty, causality, and citation boundaries calibrated to the available evidence?

anchors.1: Invents evidence or makes an unsupported ranking, causal, significance, or generalization claim.
anchors.3: Mostly respects the boundary but contains vague comparison language or an avoidable overstatement.
anchors.5: Makes comparison axes and uncertainty explicit and claims exactly what the supplied evidence supports.

rubric_dimensions.label: Reporting completeness
rubric_dimensions.question: Does the response include the information needed to interpret or reproduce the requested artifact without irrelevant additions?

anchors.1: Omits material protocol, denominator, metric, scope, or response information.
anchors.3: Includes the main information but leaves one relevant detail implicit or dependent on surrounding prose.
anchors.5: Is self-contained for the requested task and includes every relevant supplied detail without inventing others.

rubric_dimensions.label: Clarity and concision
rubric_dimensions.question: Is the prose natural, direct, cohesive, and economical rather than formulaic or model-generated sounding?

anchors.1: Is awkward, verbose, repetitive, fragmented, or difficult to parse.
anchors.3: Is readable but contains generic scaffolding, repetition, or avoidable nominalization.
anchors.5: Is concise and cohesive, with natural syntax and no sentence that can be removed without losing function.

critical_errors.label: Fabricated evidence or citation
critical_errors.description: Invents a result, experiment, source, author, venue, citation, or manuscript location.

critical_errors.label: Numeric, negation, or modality drift
critical_errors.description: Changes a number, unit, denominator, negation, uncertainty qualifier, or possibility into certainty.

critical_errors.label: Unsupported scope, causality, or ranking
critical_errors.description: Expands the tested scope or asserts causality, significance, superiority, or state of the art without support.

critical_errors.label: Comparison or protocol misreporting
critical_errors.description: Collapses incomparable settings or misstates data, metrics, trials, aggregation, hardware, training, or deployment conditions.

critical_errors.label: Source copying or quote misrepresentation
critical_errors.description: Copies source prose beyond a short unavoidable term or presents a paraphrase as a verbatim definition.
